question: Should OpenClaw expose a bounded public exec approval timeout setting, and if so what key, precedence, maximum, and security semantics should it use?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically plausible, but it changes how long host-exec approval requests remain actionable and adds public config or environment surface.

options.title: Approve bounded core config
options.body: Add one canonical timeout setting with conservative validation, maximum bounds, aligned transport/request behavior, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Keep fixed default
options.body: Leave the 30-minute default as the only supported behavior and document missed-approval recovery and fail-fast mitigations instead.

options.title: Defer to UX and fail-fast work
options.body: Improve missed-approval visibility and unsupported-surface fail-fast behavior first, then revisit configurability if operators still need it.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded core config
recommendation.body: Add one canonical timeout setting with conservative validation, maximum bounds, aligned transport/request behavior, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared timeout constant and central exec approval path trace most directly to steipete's merged feature history.
